selection: Selected publications coauthored by Minh-Ha Nguyen, linked by the medicines studied. Coverage is limited to the listed studies.

papers.title: Depression risk of 5-alpha reductase inhibitors: impact of active-comparator versus non-drug user control groups on risk measurement
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal observational studies
papers.whyRead: Examines how depression associations differ when 5-ARI users are compared with non-drug users or alpha-blocker users.
methodologicalQuestions: Do comparison groups have similar indications, disease burden and opportunities for depression diagnosis?
How much heterogeneity remains within each comparator group?
Could residual confounding affect either direction of association?
papers.interpretationLimit: Comparator-sensitive observational findings do not by themselves establish causation or the absence of adverse effects. Check the population and indication before applying a finding to a different group.

papers.title: Risk of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in New Users of 5-Alpha Reductase Inhibitors: A Nationwide Historical Cohort Study
papers.design: Nationwide new-user observational cohort in South Korea, using tamsulosin as the active comparator
papers.whyRead: Investigates incident diabetes among people treated for benign prostatic hyperplasia, using weighting to balance measured baseline risk factors.
methodologicalQuestions: Which confounders were measured, balanced by weighting or left unmeasured?
How do eligibility, lag periods and treatment discontinuation or switching affect follow-up?
Does the target population have the same indication and baseline diabetes status?
papers.interpretationLimit: The comparisons concern incident diabetes in the studied BPH population. Weighting addresses measured confounders, and the study does not establish equivalent risks or eliminate residual confounding.

papers.title: Risk of poor glycemic control in tamsulosin versus finasteride users with type 2 diabetes mellitus
papers.design: Population-based observational cohort in New Zealand comparing tamsulosin and finasteride users with existing type 2 diabetes
papers.whyRead: Addresses glycemic control in people who already have diabetes, a different outcome and population from incident-diabetes research.
methodologicalQuestions: Which medicine is the reference group for the reported effect estimate?
How was poor glycemic control defined and measured?
What range of effects remains compatible with the confidence interval?
papers.interpretationLimit: Interpret the estimate and its uncertainty together. An imprecise or non-significant comparison does not establish equivalence or an absence of effect.
